issues: Whether a proposed but unconfirmed transfer, on terms the employer had not yet agreed to, constitutes a 'reasonable alternative' the employee was required to pursue before resigning for Employment Insurance purposes

Whether the employer's failure to address workplace harassment and the proposed transfer to a different site constituted a fundamental change to the employment relationship justifying resignation (constructive dismissal)
Whether the co-workers' conduct — mocking weight and body odour, using gloves and tissue when handling items — constitutes workplace harassment under the Ontario Human Rights Code
Whether the employer failed in its duty to accommodate the employee's disability (abscess causing odour) and her recovery from ankle surgery

Whether a transfer to a different site with a longer, costlier commute, where the employee reasonably believed the same hostile environment would exist, is a reasonable alternative the employee was required to accept
Whether the employee's resignation was a reasonable response to the employer's conduct, given the employer's failure to address the harassment after being notified
The standard of review applicable to an EI decision finding that a claimant left employment without just cause
key_facts: Co-workers mocked the employee's weight and body odour and used gloves or tissue when handling items
The odour was caused by an undiagnosed abscess (a medical condition/disability)
Management spoke to the employee twice about the smell due to client complaints but did not address the harassment
The employee raised the harassment with HR and the owner; no action was taken
The employee went on medical leave during which she had ankle surgery
The employer proposed a transfer to a second site away from the harassing co-workers
The proposed transfer involved a longer and costlier commute
The employer said it would 'look at' requests for part-time hours and extra pay but had not confirmed any terms
The employee resigned before any terms were settled, believing the employer could not be trusted and the harassment would follow her
EI claim was refused on the basis that the transfer was a reasonable alternative
First-level EI appeal upheld the refusal
causes_of_action: EI just cause for leaving employment
candidate_statutes: Employment Insurance Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. E-9 (s. 34(2))
Ontario Human Rights Code, S.O. 1990, c. H.19

employer failure to address harassment resignation
